summary: F06 layout fidelity: the Key mappings and Input timings cards now share one height across all four SOCD modes. The row measures each card's natural content height and re-renders both at the taller one through a discarded sizing pass, so the two bottom edges agree exactly.

APP-CARDS-HEIGHT-MATCH.evidence: settings_cards now publishes the taller measured content height and both cards grow their frames to it with expand_to_include_rect (no item spacing), while each card publishes the natural height it measured before the stretch through context memory. the_two_settings_cards_match_height_in_every_mode asserts the two column rects share one height in all four modes (Immediate 514/514, PressDelay 489/489, RandomMix 489/489, ReleaseDelay 489/489; the shared height equals the taller card's natural frame in each mode), and the_card_row_re_measures_when_the_mode_changes asserts the row shrinks on a mode change and restores the first height on return, so the cache cannot pin a stale height. The unowned semantic flow (tests/ui_semantic.rs, untouched) still passes in the egui-ui gate.

risks: The mapping card's leftover collects below its footer instead of pushing the footer to the card's bottom edge as the reference's justify-between does; the F06 acceptance fixes matching bottom edges only, and the leftover exists only in Immediate mode, where the timing card is the taller one.

The row's shared target and the two natural heights travel through egui context memory under constant ids, because the card entry points must keep their signatures for the unowned tests/ui_semantic.rs; a second settings row on one page would share those keys.
The sizing pass uses request_discard, so a denied discard (max 2 passes) would show one stale frame, the same trade-off egui's Grid makes; once the height is stable the row runs one pass per frame.

The assigned base_commit carries the T2/T5/T6 integrations that this branch's copies of the three owned files predate; the changes here are localized (settings_cards plus one call line per card, and the new widget tests), but the integration merge still needs the Integrator's review of those files.
Native visual confirmation is outside this execution; the shared height is pinned by widget tests across the four modes, not by an on-screen session.
